title: Static hosting and deployment
learningObjectives: Explain static hosting and deployment and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: Static hosting publishes built HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and assets. A deployment workflow can validate files, build the site, run tests, and publish only after checks pass. Hosting configuration controls routing, HTTPS, headers, and caching.
understand.whyItMatters: A successful upload does not prove a release is healthy. Deployment needs validation, smoke tests, monitoring, and a rollback path.
understand.analogy: Deployment is publishing a tested package to the place users access it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The checklist lists release evidence rather than performing a deployment itself.

examples.code: const releaseChecklist=['Build succeeds','Tests pass','Assets resolve','HTTPS works','Smoke test passes','Rollback available'];console.log(releaseChecklist);
examples.explanation: The checklist lists release evidence rather than performing a deployment itself.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Prepare a deployment workflow for a static site. Include validation, build, artifact review, deployment, and post-deploy smoke tests.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
